picks.d: SF's hottest EDM festival returns to Pier 80 with an absolutely stacked lineup — Robyn, Fatboy Slim, and Dog Blood on Saturday; Swedish House Mafia, Tiësto, and Four Tet on Sunday. This is the one everyone's been talking about all summer, so don't sleep on it.

The world's largest leather and kink street fair takes over SoMa — 400,000 people, free entry, and an energy that's completely unlike anything else in the city. Whether you're a regular or a first-timer, this is one of SF's most iconic annual moments.

The full lineup is already announced and the buzz is real — SF's beloved free festival in Golden Gate Park is almost here. Use this week to plan your days, grab snacks, and rally your crew because it kicks off Friday Oct 2.

picks.t: Giants vs. Dodgers — Final Home Stand
picks.d: The Giants close out the regular season at Oracle Park against the Dodgers — their biggest NL West rival — in what could be a playoff-seeding showdown. Buy a ticket and you'll also score a 2027 ticket voucher. This is the last home baseball of 2026, folks.

picks.t: Sleep — Two Nights at the Fillmore
picks.d: The doom-metal legends bring their North America 2026 tour to one of SF's most hallowed stages for back-to-back nights of colossal riffs and hypnotic heaviness. If you've ever wanted to feel a bassline in your actual bones, this is your moment.

Beck at The Masonic is always a treat — he's famous for skipping the obvious hits and throwing in deep cuts and surprises that make every show feel genuinely fresh. Two nights means two totally different setlists, so honestly, go both nights if you can swing it.

picks.t: Ha Chong-Hyun Retrospective Opens — Asian Art Museum
picks.d: One of Korea's most celebrated modern artists gets a major retrospective at the Asian Art Museum, opening this Thursday. His revolutionary Hanji paintings are breathtaking in person, and this pairs beautifully with the RM x SFMOMA show coming next week for a full Korean art moment in SF.

picks.t: Sunset Night Market — Autumn Moon Festival
picks.d: The Sunset District's beloved night market is back at Irving & 22nd with DJs, dance performances, international food trucks, and all the neighborhood dumpling-shop vibes you love — themed around the Autumn Moon Festival. It's free, it's festive, and it's the perfect Friday warm-up.

Jack White hits Bill Graham Civic Auditorium on a creative hot streak — setlists that are never fixed, moods that shift from full-throttle garage stomp to stripped-down ballad on a dime. No two White shows are alike, and that's exactly the point.

picks.w: Thu Sep 25 – Sat Sep 27 · All Day
picks.d: The 20th anniversary of Maker Faire is happening at the historic Mare Island Shipyard — think wild inventions, tech art, robotics, and creative chaos at a shipyard you can reach by ferry. It's equal parts inspiring and genuinely weird, in the best way.

picks.t: Northwest by Northwest — A.C.T. at Toni Rembe Theater
picks.d: Emma Rice's theatrical adaptation of Hitchcock's classic spy-caper thriller is the season opener for A.C.T. — expect action set pieces, snappy one-liners, and the kind of sparky romance that makes you wish every date night involved a cross-country murder plot.

picks.t: Dolly Day SF — Free Tribute at Union Square
picks.d: A free, community-organized celebration of Dolly Parton descends on Union Square with live music, tributes, and maximum glam. You don't need a reason to love Dolly, but if you did — this is it.

picks.t: Free Shakespeare: Antony and Cleopatra — Final Weekend
picks.d: This is your last chance to catch Free Shakespeare in the Park's 44th season — Antony and Cleopatra at Sue Bierman Park, no tickets needed. Pack a blanket, grab a coffee, and let the drama unfold.

picks.t: Jack Johnson + G. Love — Greek Theatre Berkeley
picks.d: Both nights are sold out, but resale is your friend — catching Jack Johnson at the Greek is one of those quintessential Bay Area fall evenings. G. Love opens, the eucalyptus smells amazing, and the vibes are immaculate.

ongoing.t: de Young: A Gallery of Their Own + Monet and Venice
ongoing.d: Two strong shows running simultaneously — catch Monet's Venetian views alongside a compelling group exhibition. Free first Tuesdays.
Month-long artist open-studio crawl kicks off Sep 26; browse studios across the city through October 25, totally free.

ongoing.t: SF Symphony Fall Season — Davies Symphony Hall
ongoing.d: World-class classical programming in Hayes Valley; check sfsymphony.org for this week's specific program.
Susi Damilano's comedic take on the classic Barrie story is running now; expect big laughs and a wild trip to Neverland.

new.name: Yumee Katsu
new.d: SF's first outpost of the beloved mini-chain — fish, pork, and cheese-stuffed katsu plus noodles and curry. A neighborhood instant classic.

new.type: Indian Coffee Shop · Lower Nob Hill
new.name: Le Mil's
new.d: One of SF's only Indian cafés — order the chicory coffee with masala jaggery syrup and grab a pastry from Saltwater Bakeshop.

new.name: Sourdough Tartine Café
new.d: Inside Tartine's production facility — ube sourdough tartines with ube mascarpone cream, gochujang kimchi grilled cheese, and great coffee.

new.name: Duke's Smash & Scoop
new.d: Classic smashburgers done right, with Double Rainbow milkshakes to seal the deal. Perfect post-show fuel on Haight Street.

new.name: New Chinese Spot, Mission Bay
new.d: Open sliding doors onto Mission Creek, fire-pit patio seating, and standouts like pineapple bun with duck pâté and Sichuan prawn cocktail.

classic.name: City View Restaurant
classic.d: Old-school cart dim sum in a bright, airy room — go at lunch on Saturday before the Giants game.

classic.name: La Taqueria
classic.d: James Beard Award–winning burritos with no rice, all flavor — the Mission benchmark since 1973.

classic.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
classic.d: World-champion Neapolitan pizza in the heart of North Beach — pre-game fuel before a Cobb's comedy show.

classic.name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
classic.d: Sustainably farmed West Coast oysters right on the Ferry Building waterfront — a perfect pre-concert ritual.

classic.name: Marufuku Ramen
classic.d: Rich Hakata-style tonkotsu broth with perfectly springy noodles — expect a line, worth every minute.

classic.name: Zazie
classic.d: The quintessential SF neighborhood brunch spot — French-inspired, charming garden patio, and a bottomless option that earns its reputation.

bars.name: Smuggler's Cove
bars.d: Three floors of tiki excess and 500+ rum options — order the Zombie and surrender to the vibe.

bars.name: Zeitgeist
bars.d: Massive sunny beer garden, cold pitchers, no pretense — the platonic ideal of a SF dive bar.

bars.name: The Riddler
bars.d: All-Champagne wine bar with a chic, welcoming room — great for a pre-show toast or a low-key Friday night.

bars.name: Cellarmaker Brewing
bars.d: Some of the most sought-after IPAs in the city, poured fresh at their SoMa taproom.

bars.name: Monarch
bars.d: Gorgeous multi-level nightclub and bar just outside SoMa proper — great cocktails early, great DJs late.

bars.name: Toronado
bars.d: Beer nerd paradise with 50+ rotating taps — the perfect post-Duke's Smash & Scoop nightcap.

bars.name: Charmaine's at the Proper Hotel
bars.d: The city's best rooftop view with solid cocktails — ideal for a pre-show drink before anything downtown.

bars.name: Vesuvio Café
bars.d: Legendary Beat Generation bar next to City Lights — order a cheap beer and soak in the literary ghosts.

games.detail: Final home series of the regular season — potential playoff implications
Afternoon rivalry game at the ballpark
Last home game of 2026 — don't miss it

sports.note: Buy any September home game ticket and receive a 2027 ticket voucher. The Dodgers entered this week at 93–60 — this series matters.

games.detail: Valkyries (31–11, 2nd in Western Conference) are on the road this week. Playoff presale tickets are live now.

sports.note: Grab Valkyries playoff tickets now while presale is active — this team is for real.

concerts.d: No set list is ever fixed with Jack White — he veers from raw garage-rock thunder to warped blues to stripped-down ballads within a single show. Bill Graham Civic Auditorium is the perfect room for his unpredictable energy.

Beck is the rare artist who flips from slacker anthems to lush genre experiments without missing a beat — and he's notorious for skipping the obvious hits in favor of deep cuts. Two nights at The Masonic means two totally different adventures.

Two nights of colossal doom-metal riffs and hypnotic, meditative heaviness at one of SF's most storied stages. If you've never experienced Sleep live, prepare for deep sludgy guitar tones and thunderous drums that feel genuinely physical.
Joanne McNally brings her sharp, self-aware comedy to Cobb's for three shows this weekend. She's the kind of comic who makes the whole room feel like they're in on the joke together.
A late-night underground set at one of SF's most storied intimate rooms — exactly the kind of show you discover and tell everyone about for years. Check GAMH's box office for pricing and details.

concerts.t: Rusty Chains — Tribute to Chris Cornell
concerts.d: An intimate, heartfelt tribute to one of rock's greatest voices — Soundgarden, Audioslave, and Cornell's solo catalogue performed live at the Great American Music Hall. If you grew up with those records, bring tissues.

The influential post-hardcore songwriter behind Jawbox and Burning Airlines brings his emotionally resonant catalog to The Warfield. A quieter Saturday pick for the music nerds who know — and they know.

concerts.t: Jack Johnson + G. Love — SURFILMUSIC Tour
concerts.d: Both nights at the Greek are sold out, but this is the kind of show where hunting for resale tickets is absolutely worth it. An outdoor evening at one of the Bay's most beautiful amphitheaters with the most laid-back acoustic sound on the planet.
concerts.venue: Greek Theatre, Berkeley · Resale Only (SOLD OUT)

concerts.d: A Thursday-night closer at the beloved Great American Music Hall — the perfect way to cap an absolutely packed week of live music in SF. Check GAMH's site for ticket details.

concertsOngoing.t: SF Symphony Fall Season — Davies Symphony Hall
concertsOngoing.d: World-class programming including renowned soloists; check sfsymphony.org for this week's specific program.

concertsOngoing.t: SF Electronic Music Festival (SFEMF) — THE LAB
concertsOngoing.d: Experimental and avant-garde electronic artists at THE LAB on 16th St through September 25.

singles.d: Meet 8–12 local singles in one fun, structured evening at Blackbird — multiple age brackets available so you can find your crowd. It's low-stakes, surprisingly fun, and way better than swiping.

singles.t: Lock & Key Singles Mixer — Bay Area
singles.d: Women get keys, men get locks, and everyone mingles while trying to unlock each other's mystery padlock — it's a genuinely clever icebreaker that forces conversation in the best way. Way more fun than standing around a bar hoping someone talks to you.

singles.t: Volo Sports — Glow Kickball + Flip Cup (Coed)
singles.d: Sign up as a free agent and Volo places you on a team — you'll play glow-in-the-dark kickball at Dolores Park and then face off in Flip Cup at a sponsor bar after the game. Countless SF relationships have started exactly this way.

singles.t: Run Club SF — Weekly Group Runs
singles.w: Tue / Thu / Fri / Sat · Various Times
singles.d: Tuesday wildcard runs through Golden Gate Park, Thursday speedwork at Kezar Stadium, Friday trail runs in the Marin Headlands, Saturday adventure runs around the city — free to join and genuinely community-first. Countless friendships (and more) have started here.

singles.w: Sat Sep 26 & Sun Sep 27 · All Day
singles.d: Pier 80 with tens of thousands of people dancing to Robyn, Swedish House Mafia, Tiësto, and Four Tet — it's basically the city's biggest singles event of the fall, just with better music. Go with friends or go solo; you'll find your people on the dance floor.

A clean, classic speed dating format for the 25–45 crowd — Bay Area Speed Dating runs regular Thursday and weekend events across the city. It's efficient, it's fun, and you'll walk out having had more real conversations than a week of app swiping.

singlesOngoing.d: Neighborhood-first run crew with a relaxed, welcoming vibe — great for social miles and meeting people.
Coed 6v6 leagues at Mission High and SF International HS; sign up as a free agent.

singlesOngoing.t: Volo Pickleball Tournament — Sundays at The Crossing
singlesOngoing.d: Coed pickleball at the East Cut — great for meeting competitive-but-fun people on the courts.

date.title: Shakespeare, Sunset, and Dolly
date.tagline: A full free afternoon-to-evening with serious charm.

steps.title: Free Shakespeare in the Park
steps.detail: Catch Antony and Cleopatra at Sue Bierman Park — it's the final weekend of the 44th season. Bring a blanket and let the drama do the heavy lifting.

steps.title: Walk the Embarcadero
steps.detail: Stroll south from the park along the waterfront. Stop at the Ferry Building for a sample or two — the cheese counter at Cowgirl Creamery never disappoints.

steps.title: Sunset Night Market at Irving & 22nd
steps.detail: Hop a Muni out to the Sunset District for the Autumn Moon Festival Night Market — free entry, live DJs, dance performances, and a dozen food options. This is the move.

date.title: Oysters, Beck, and a Late-Night Dive
date.tagline: Dinner at the Ferry Building, then Beck at The Masonic.

steps.title: Hog Island Oyster Co. — Embarcadero
steps.detail: Start with a dozen West Coast oysters at the Ferry Building waterfront bar. Order the mignonette, split a bottle of something cold, and take your time.

steps.title: Walk up to The Masonic
steps.detail: It's a scenic uphill walk or a quick Lyft to Nob Hill — either way, you'll arrive right as Beck is about to start at 7:30pm.

steps.title: Beck — Ride Lonesome Tour at The Masonic
steps.detail: Friday or Saturday night — both are great. Let Beck's genre-bending setlist surprise you both and give you something to talk about after.

steps.title: Nightcap at Vesuvio, North Beach
steps.detail: End the night at the legendary Beat-era bar on Columbus Ave — cheap drinks, incredible atmosphere, and the best kind of low-key conversation spot to close out a great date.

date.title: Mission Bay Waterfront Dinner + Portola Festival
date.tagline: The most memorable Saturday night of the year.

steps.title: New Chinese-Leaning Spot, Mission Bay
steps.detail: Snag a patio table by Mission Creek — fire pits, open sliding doors, and a menu full of conversation starters like the pineapple bun with duck pâté and Sichuan prawn cocktail.

steps.title: Head to Pier 80 — Portola Festival
steps.detail: It's a short ride to the festival grounds. Saturday's headliners include Robyn and Fatboy Slim — you will absolutely be dancing by 9pm.

steps.title: Dance All Night
steps.detail: Dog Blood and Soulwax are also on the bill — drift between stages, find your favorite, and just enjoy the fact that you're at the best party in the city tonight.

solo.title: The Full Free Culture Saturday
solo.tagline: Art, Shakespeare, and a street fair. All free. All SF.

steps.title: Ha Chong-Hyun Retrospective — Asian Art Museum
steps.detail: Opening weekend of a major Korean modern art retrospective — arrive early on Saturday to beat the crowds. Free for Bay Area residents with valid ID.

steps.title: Grab Lunch in the Civic Center
steps.detail: Fuel up at a nearby taqueria or food truck before the afternoon activities kick in.

steps.title: Free Shakespeare — Sue Bierman Park
steps.detail: Antony and Cleopatra, final weekend. Bring sunscreen and a snack and let the afternoon drift.

steps.title: SF Open Studios Crawl Begins
steps.detail: The month-long citywide open studios event kicks off this weekend — pick a neighborhood and start exploring. You never know what you'll find or who you'll meet.

solo.title: Sleep at the Fillmore — A Night for Yourself
solo.tagline: Great food solo, then doom metal in one of SF's best rooms.

steps.title: Dinner at Marufuku Ramen
steps.detail: Solo ramen is genuinely one of life's great pleasures — rich tonkotsu broth, springy noodles, and nobody to share your chashu with. Go early to beat the line.

steps.title: Walk to The Fillmore
steps.detail: Pick up your Apple Bag on the way in — the Fillmore's poster collection from past shows is displayed throughout, and browsing it solo is its own kind of pleasure.

steps.title: Sleep — North America 2026
steps.detail: Let the riffs wash over you. Sleep's music is made for exactly this — closing your eyes, losing track of time, and feeling genuinely tiny in the best possible way.

solo.title: Giants Finale + Rooftop + Comedy
solo.tagline: A full solo day that hits every SF note.

steps.title: Pre-Game at Zazie Brunch — Hayes Valley
steps.detail: A leisurely solo brunch before an afternoon at the ballpark — treat yourself to the bottomless option and take your time with a book or the game-day paper.

steps.title: Giants vs. Dodgers — Saturday Afternoon at Oracle
steps.detail: Last home series of the season against the Dodgers. Grab a great seat, soak in the McCovey Cove views, and cheer loud.

steps.title: Charmaine's Rooftop at the Proper Hotel
steps.detail: Post-game sunset cocktail with a panoramic city view. Treat yourself — you earned it.

steps.title: Joanne McNally: Pinotphile — Cobb's Comedy Club
steps.detail: End the night with laughs at one of SF's best comedy clubs. Solo comedy shows are wildly underrated — you'll laugh harder when there's no one to nudge.

birthday.title: The Outdoor Birthday Sweep
birthday.tagline: Dolly, the night market, and Shakespeare — all free, all fun.

steps.title: Free Shakespeare — Sue Bierman Park
steps.detail: Kick off the birthday afternoon with Antony and Cleopatra in the park. Bring the group, bring a blanket, bring birthday snacks.

steps.title: Dolly Day SF — Union Square
steps.detail: Head to Union Square for the free Dolly Parton tribute celebration — live music, glam, and community joy. Perfect birthday energy.

steps.title: Sunset Night Market — Irving & 22nd
steps.detail: Finish the free portion of the evening at the Autumn Moon Festival Night Market in the Sunset. DJs, food trucks, dance performances — the birthday crew will love it.

birthday.title: Beck Friday — The Classic SF Birthday Night
birthday.tagline: Dinner in Hayes Valley, then Beck at The Masonic.

steps.title: Birthday Dinner — Hayes Valley
steps.detail: Book a table somewhere you love in Hayes Valley — it's perfectly positioned between the pre-game drinks scene and The Masonic. Let the birthday person pick the restaurant.

steps.title: Beck — Ride Lonesome Tour
steps.detail: Get there for the start — Beck's openers are part of the experience. The Masonic is a beautiful room for a birthday night, and the setlist surprises will be a shared memory.

steps.title: Late-Night at Toronado — The Haight
steps.detail: 50+ rotating taps and zero pretense — the perfect post-show birthday bar. Order something weird and celebrate properly.

birthday.title: Giants Series + Portola + VIP Dinner
birthday.tagline: The biggest possible birthday weekend in SF.

steps.title: Giants vs. Dodgers — Oracle Park
steps.detail: Afternoon game with the crew — grab great seats, split some garlic fries, and soak in the final home series of the season. Get the birthday person a ballpark cupcake.

steps.title: Mission Bay Waterfront Dinner — The New Chinese Spot
steps.detail: Firepit patio table by Mission Creek — this is the dinner the birthday person will be talking about. The pineapple bun and duck pâté alone are worth the trip.

steps.title: Portola Festival — Pier 80
steps.detail: Robyn, Fatboy Slim, Dog Blood, Soulwax — this is the birthday night everyone wanted. Dance until you physically cannot anymore.

friends.title: Circus, Shakespeare, and a Night Market
friends.tagline: Pack your whole Saturday with free outdoor fun.

steps.title: Circus on the Square — St. Mark's Square
steps.detail: Circus Bella performs free acrobatics, juggling, and aerial acts from 11am–2pm — plus free popcorn. An unexpectedly great group activity.

steps.title: Free Shakespeare — Sue Bierman Park
steps.detail: Roll over to the final weekend of Antony and Cleopatra. It's free, it's outdoors, and it gives you something to dramatically quote at each other for the rest of the day.

steps.title: Sunset Night Market — Irving & 22nd Ave
steps.detail: End the free portion at the Autumn Moon Festival Night Market — split food truck orders, argue about which dumpling place is best, and let the DJs do their thing.

steps.title: Dive Bar Finish at Zeitgeist
steps.detail: Cold pitchers, picnic tables, and good company in the Mission beer garden. This is how the night ends.

friends.title: Giants + Comedy Night
friends.tagline: Baseball by day, Cobb's by night — the quintessential SF crew day.

steps.title: Pre-Game Brunch — North Beach
steps.detail: Meet up at Tony's Pizza Napoletana or a North Beach café before heading toward the ballpark. Get the group caffeinated and fed.

steps.title: Giants vs. Dodgers — Oracle Park
steps.detail: Saturday afternoon at Oracle is a ritual — garlic fries are mandatory, rivalry energy is high, and you'll have plenty to talk about afterward.

steps.title: Post-Game Drinks — The Embarcadero
steps.detail: Walk up to Hog Island for a round of oysters and post-game analysis. Argue about the game. Order another round.

steps.title: Joanne McNally: Pinotphile — Cobb's Comedy Club
steps.detail: Cap the night with live comedy in North Beach — Saturday has a 7pm and 9:15pm show, so you've got options depending on how long the oyster round stretches.

friends.title: Maker Faire by Ferry + Portola Weekend
friends.tagline: A two-day crew adventure that covers maximum ground.

steps.title: Ferry to Maker Faire at Mare Island
steps.detail: Take the ferry to the 20th Anniversary Maker Faire at the historic Mare Island Shipyard — wild inventions, tech art, and creative chaos. It's genuinely unlike anything else.

steps.title: Return to SF — Refresh and Pregame
steps.detail: Head back across the bay, get changed, grab a solid dinner, and get ready for the main event.

steps.title: Portola Music Festival — Pier 80
steps.detail: Robyn, Fatboy Slim, Dog Blood, Soulwax on Saturday night. This is it. Dance together until the lights come up.

steps.title: Recovery Brunch + Folsom Street Fair
steps.detail: Sunday brings Swedish House Mafia and Tiësto at Portola — but first, brunch and a walk through the Folsom Street Fair, which is completely free and an SF experience in itself.

parents.title: Circus, Park, and Night Market
parents.tagline: A perfect free Saturday the whole family will remember.

steps.title: Circus on the Square — St. Mark's Square
steps.detail: Free circus performances from Circus Bella from 11am–2pm with free popcorn for the kids. Acrobatics, juggling, aerial acts — this is the kind of thing kids talk about for weeks.

steps.title: Lunch in the Neighborhood
steps.detail: Grab something nearby — it's a great opportunity to try a neighborhood spot you've been meaning to visit.

steps.title: de Young Museum — Golden Gate Park
steps.detail: Walk or Uber over to the de Young to see Monet and Venice and A Gallery of Their Own. Free for Bay Area residents on the first Tuesday — or check the Saturday free hours.

steps.title: Sunset Night Market — Irving & 22nd Ave
steps.detail: A gentle walk from Golden Gate Park to the Sunset for the Autumn Moon Festival Night Market — family-friendly, festive, and free to enter.

parents.title: Maker Faire Day Trip + City Dinner
parents.tagline: A genuinely exciting adventure for curious families.

steps.title: Ferry to Mare Island — Maker Faire
steps.detail: The 20th Anniversary Maker Faire at the historic Mare Island Shipyard is accessible by car or ferry — the ferry ride alone is an adventure. Tickets run $28–$84 depending on age.

steps.title: Explore the Maker Faire
steps.detail: Robotics, inventions, 3D printing, art installations, demonstrations — give the kids (and yourselves) a full afternoon to wander and get inspired.

steps.title: Ferry Back to SF
steps.detail: Return to the city with plenty of time to decompress before dinner.

steps.title: Dinner at Yumee Katsu — Lower Pacific Heights
steps.detail: SF's first outpost of the beloved katsu mini-chain — fish, pork, and cheese-stuffed katsu, noodles, and curry. Kid-friendly, affordable, and genuinely delicious.

parents.title: Giants Weekend + Art + Waterfront Dinner
parents.tagline: The full SF family experience in one beautiful weekend.

steps.title: Ha Chong-Hyun Retrospective — Asian Art Museum
steps.detail: Opening weekend of a major Korean modern art survey — a genuinely exciting thing to experience together as a family, especially paired with talking about what's happening in SF art right now.

steps.title: Giants vs. Dodgers — Oracle Park
steps.detail: Saturday afternoon baseball against the Dodgers in the last home series of the year — garlic fries, the bay views, and the playoff-race energy make this a perfect family ballpark day.

steps.title: Waterfront Dinner — Mission Bay
steps.detail: The new Chinese-leaning waterfront restaurant by Mission Creek has firepit patio seating and a menu full of interesting, shareable dishes. A great way to end a full day together.

steps.title: Giants vs. Dodgers — Sunday Finale at Oracle
steps.detail: If you loved Saturday, Sunday's noon game is a perfect quieter follow-up — earlier start, relaxed afternoon game atmosphere, and the last Giants home game of 2026.
